summary: cchsflow's working-tree NAMESPACE exports 125 symbols (task brief said 127; two were dropped in the uncommitted repair). The surface is a three-generation accretion: 27 legacy *_fun/_fun1/_fun2 exports, 51 verb-prefixed v3 exports (calculate_/assess_/categorize_/score_/adjust_), 6 bare CCHS-name doc placeholders, ~30 engine/cache internals (is_equal, if_else2, cache_pattern, apply_database_heuristics...), and 24 exported functions that are not functions at all -- 18 unconditionally stop('DOCUMENTATION ONLY') and 6 have empty bodies. rec_with_table has 11 parameters of which 3 (else_value, append_to_data, custom_function_path) are used in zero of 291 repo call sites and 2 have doc-vs-code default mismatches. Error messaging is pre-cli/rlang base-R paste(): typos ('varLalbel', 'more then once'), raw source indentation printed to console, vectorized paste() warning mash, and one bare 'Invalid Argument was passed'; the package's own man pages wrap examples in suppressWarnings() 23 times. DV dispatch is positional (unname + do.call), making worksheet argument order a silent-corruption hazard. Docs infra is broken: _pkgdown.yml still indexes deleted functions (bmi_fun et al.), omits 90/125 current exports, and vignettes still teach bmi_fun. 32 exports have no examples and 49 only \dontrun. These findings directly substantiate the recodeflow scoping complaints (too many parameters, not enough logging/why-failure context) and define the v4 API cleanup scope.

issues.title: 24 exported 'functions' are documentation-only placeholders (18 always error, 6 empty bodies)
evidence: R/smoking-status.R:92-93 calculate_SMKDSTY_cat5 <- function(data, output_format=...) { stop("DOCUMENTATION ONLY: Use rec_with_table(data, 'SMKDSTY_cat5') for implementation") }
18 stop('DOCUMENTATION ONLY') stubs, all exported: smoking-status.R:93,145,197,250,306; smoke-stop.R:74,120,153,183; smoke-start.R:102,163,304,546,592; smoke-intensity.R:209,250,286,322
R/depression.R:27-29 'DPSDSF <- function(DPSDSF) { # this is for documentation purposes only }' -- exported, empty body, roxygen says 'NOTE: this is not a function'

R/life-satisfaction.R:44-46 GEN_02A2 <- function(GEN_02A, GEN_02A2) {}; R/occupation.R:36-38,82,124 LBFA_31A/_a/_b same pattern; 14 occurrences of 'documentation purposes only'/'not a function' across R/
Two exports carry a '_stub' suffix in the public API: calculate_time_quit_smoking_complete_stub (R/smoke-stop.R:149), calculate_time_quit_smoking_daily_stub (R/smoke-stop.R:180)
Net: 24/125 exports (19%) error or no-op when called; functions are also named identically to their own first parameter (DPSDSF(DPSDSF))
issues.why_design_issue: An exported function is a contract that it can be called. Users autocomplete calculate_SMK_204(), call it, and get an unconditional error; DPSDSF() silently returns NULL. This abuses the function namespace as a documentation system for worksheet-implemented variables, inflates the API ~19%, and forces every stub to fake a signature (data, output_format) it never uses.
issues.candidate_fix: v4: document worksheet-implemented variables as data/topic docs (roxygen @name + @docType or pkgdown articles auto-generated from variables.csv), not exported closures. Delete the 18 stop-stubs and 6 empty bodies from NAMESPACE; keep .Rd topics via @name pages so ?SMKDSTY_cat5 still works.

issues.title: Three coexisting naming generations across the 125 exports, mirrored inside the worksheet
evidence: NAMESPACE: 43 calculate_*, 8 assess_/categorize_/score_/adjust_*, 27 *_fun|_fun1|_fun2|_fun_cat (e.g. pack_years_fun, CCC_091_fun1, multiple_conditions_fun3), 1 *_der (food_insecurity_der), 6 bare CCHS names (DPSDPP, DPSDSF, GEN_02A2, LBFA_31A, LBFA_31A_a, LBFA_31A_b)

Both generations of the same concept exported simultaneously: pack_years_fun (R/smoking.R:266, CCHS-code params) AND calculate_pack_years (R/smoke-pack-years.R:120, semantic params); smoke_simple_fun AND calculate_smoke_simple; time_quit_smoking_fun AND calculate_time_quit_smoking

inst/extdata/variable_details.csv recEnd Func:: references mix vocabularies: 46 distinct functions, ~17 *_fun-style (active_transport1_fun, diet_score_fun, RACDPAL_fun) vs ~28 verb-style (calculate_bmi, assess_adl, categorize_immigration)

Numbered-variant suffixes carry no meaning to users: CCC_091_fun1 vs CCC_091_fun2, COPD_Emph_der_fun1/2, multiple_conditions_fun1/2/3, resp_condition_fun (suffix-less survivor after fun1/2/3 deleted per git status man/resp_condition_fun[123].Rd)
issues.why_design_issue: Users cannot predict a function name (is BMI bmi_fun, calculate_bmi, or HWTGBMI?), and the worksheet's Func:: strings hard-couple both generations into the engine via get(), so neither can be removed without a coordinated worksheet+NAMESPACE migration. Numbered _fun1/_fun2 variants encode era logic in opaque suffixes the team has already agreed to deprecate (era-split naming feedback).
issues.candidate_fix: v4: single verb_noun convention (the calculate_/assess_/categorize_ family), one exported function per concept; era variants become internal dispatch or year-suffixed names (_pre2015/_2015plus). Keep *_fun as deprecated shims for one release with lifecycle::deprecate_warn, and migrate worksheet Func:: strings in the same change-set.

issues.title: rec_with_table: 11 parameters, 3 never used anywhere in the repo, 2 with doc-vs-code default mismatches
evidence: R/recode-with-table.R:154-165 signature: data, variables, database_name, variable_details, else_value, append_to_data, log, notes, var_labels, custom_function_path, attach_data_name (11 params)
Usage across 291 rec_with_table() call sites in vignettes/ + tests/: log= 22, var_labels= 4, notes= 3, attach_data_name= 2, else_value= 0, append_to_data= 0, custom_function_path= 0
Doc/default mismatch 1: R/recode-with-table.R:113-114 '@param append_to_data Logical, if TRUE (default)' vs line 160 'append_to_data = FALSE'
Doc/default mismatch 2: R/recode-with-table.R:117-118 '@param notes Logical, if FALSE (default), will not print' vs line 162 'notes = TRUE'
/tmp/recodeflow-pr43/index.qmd:39 lists 'The function having too many parameters (complex API)' as a named v-next driver
R/recode-with-table.R:167-169: custom_function_path is implemented as bare source(path) -- comment claims 'create new environment and source' but source() defaults to the global environment
issues.why_design_issue: More than half the parameter list is dead weight or wrong: 3 of 11 options have zero observed usage, and the two most behaviour-changing flags (append_to_data, notes) are documented with inverted defaults, so a user reading ?rec_with_table gets the opposite of what the code does. custom_function_path silently pollutes the caller's global environment.
issues.candidate_fix: Immediate: fix the two @param default descriptions (S). v4: core signature rec_with_table(data, variables, database, variable_details) with secondary options moved to a control object or dedicated verbs (attach labels via label step; logging via logger config per the recodeflow logging scope); replace custom_function_path with an explicit functions= named list evaluated in a child environment.

issues.title: Error/warning messages are pre-cli base paste(): typos, printed source indentation, vectorized message mash, non-actionable text
evidence: Zero cli::/rlang::abort()/error-class usage in R/ (grep across 123 stop()/warning() calls found none)

1. R/recode-with-table.R:297-300 stop('The passed labels was not a named vector please follow\n the c(var_name = varLalbel) format') -- typo 'varLalbel', run-on, embedded newline+10-space indent printed verbatim

2. R/recode-with-table.R:394-409 stop(paste('The row\n ', row, 'for the variable', ..., 'Does not contain the database being checked(', data_name, ') in its variable start the default is also missing...')) -- broken spacing, raw indentation, unclear remedy
3. R/recode-with-table.R:497-504 stop(paste(single_from, 'was detected more then once in', ...)) -- typo 'then'
4. R/recode-with-table.R:529-536 stop(paste(variable, ' contains', n, 'rows of else only one else value is allowed')) -- run-on, double space
5. R/recode-with-table.R:750 stop('Invalid Argument was passed') -- no argument name, no function, no expected values
6. R/recode-with-table.R:233-241 stop('The passed number of data does not match the passed number of\n data_names. ... Aborting operation!') -- multi-line literal prints leading whitespace

7. R/recode-with-table.R:279-284 warning(paste(missing_vars, 'is missing from variable details therefore cannot be recoded')) -- paste() vectorizes over missing_vars producing repeated mashed text; 'is' vs 'are'
8. R/recode-with-table.R:870-878 warning(paste(variable, 'could not be derived because', feeder_vars, 'was never specified...\n')) -- vectorized over feeder_vars, embedded \n and indentation

9. R/number-conditions.R (CCC_091_fun1) lines 38-46: warning(paste('In CCC_91A:', CCC_91A, ..., sep = '')) -- sep='' concatenates words together AND fires once per data row via rowwise dispatch (warning floods on real datasets)

10. Contrast (good, v3): R/missing-pattern-cache.R:85 stop("Variable '", variable_name, "' not found in cache. Use has_cached_pattern() first.") -- actionable; shows the package already has the better style in newer files
Consequence: package suppresses its own diagnostics -- 23 man/*.Rd wrap examples in suppressWarnings(); 65 suppressWarnings/suppressMessages across vignettes/R/man
issues.why_design_issue: The recodeflow scoping doc's top complaint is 'users not knowing why a function failure has taken place'. Messages with typos, raw indentation, vectorized mash and 'Invalid Argument was passed' make failures undiagnosable, and the per-row warning pattern trains users (and the package's own examples) to suppressWarnings(), hiding real data problems in a health-data harmonization tool where silent miscoding is a methodological-defensibility risk.
issues.candidate_fix: v4: adopt cli::cli_abort/cli_warn with error classes (cchsflow_error_missing_variable, etc.), one aggregated warning per variable (not per row) carrying counts and affected databases, and a structured log per the recodeflow logging scope. Short term: fix typos and de-vectorize paste() calls in rec_with_table (S).

issues.title: DerivedVar dispatch strips argument names: worksheet column order silently maps to positional formals
evidence: R/recode-with-table.R:978-980: row_values <- unname(row_values); do.call(get(custom_function_name), row_values)
get(custom_function_name) resolves by bare string lookup on the search path -- no namespace qualification, no existence pre-check with informative error
Contract is only documented by convention: DerivedVar::[HWTGHTM, HWTGWTK] order must equal calculate_bmi(height_m, weight_kg) formals order; swapping them computes weight/height^2 silently

DV functions cannot be argument-defaulted safely: calculate_pack_years (R/smoke-pack-years.R:120-129) has 4 optional NULL params + output_format that positional dispatch can clobber if worksheet passes more vars than expected
issues.why_design_issue: The only protection against transposed inputs is human review of CSV cell order against function source. For a package whose purpose is correctness of harmonized estimates, an order-typo produces plausible wrong numbers rather than an error -- the worst failure mode. It also blocks evolving signatures (any new parameter must go last forever).
issues.candidate_fix: v4 engine: match worksheet variable names to function formals by name (do.call with named list), validate setequal(names, formals) at recode time, and error with the offending variable list. Where DV functions use semantic param names, add an explicit args-mapping column or require named DerivedVar::[height_m = HWTGHTM, ...] syntax.

issues.title: pkgdown index and vignettes reference deleted functions; 90/125 current exports missing from reference index
evidence: _pkgdown.yml:64-88 still lists bmi_fun, adjusted_bmi_fun, bmi_fun_cat, resp_condition_fun1, binge_drinker_fun, adl_fun, low_drink_short_fun, low_drink_long_fun, low_drink_score_fun, low_drink_score_fun1 -- all of whose man/*.Rd are deleted in the working tree (git status: D man/bmi_fun.Rd, D man/adl_fun.Rd, ...)
90 of 125 exports absent from _pkgdown.yml reference section, including the entire v3 surface (calculate_bmi, assess_adl, clean_variables, rec_with_table helpers, all 18 getters)
vignettes/derived_variables.Rmd:21,42 teaches 'Func::bmi_fun' and reproduces bmi_fun source -- function no longer exists
vignettes/tagged_na_usage.Rmd:92 hard-links https://big-life-lab.github.io/cchsflow/reference/bmi_fun.html -- will 404 after rebuild
issues.why_design_issue: pkgdown build fails (or silently drops topics) when the reference index cites missing topics, so the public docs site cannot be rebuilt from this tree; the flagship derived-variables vignette teaches an API that errors. This is the embarrassment scenario: docs contradict the package on its own headline feature.
issues.candidate_fix: Regenerate _pkgdown.yml reference section from NAMESPACE groups (one section per naming family), update the two vignettes to calculate_bmi and the v3 3-step story, and add a CI step that runs pkgdown::check_pkgdown().

issues.title: Inconsistent parameter vocabulary across DV functions: semantic names vs raw CCHS codes, and uneven output_format
evidence: Semantic: calculate_bmi(height_m, weight_kg) R/bmi.R:82; adjust_bmi(sex, height_m, weight_kg) R/bmi.R:187; calculate_pct_time(age, born_in_canada, years_in_canada) R/percent-time-canada.R:59; categorize_immigration(immigrant_status, born_canada, ethnicity, ...) R/immigration.R:56; calculate_pack_years(smoking_status, age, age_start_smoking, ...) R/smoke-pack-years.R:120

Raw CCHS codes in the same generation: calculate_binge_drinking(DHH_SEX, ALW_1, ALW_2A1..ALW_2A7) R/alcohol.R:182-184; assess_adl(ADL_01..ADL_05) R/adl.R:89; calculate_SMKG203_cont(SMK_005, SMKG040_cont) R/smoke-start.R:224
Same concept, two vocabularies: pack_years_fun(SMKDSTY_original, DHHGAGE_cont, time_quit_smoking, SMKG203_cont, ...) R/smoking.R:266 vs calculate_pack_years(smoking_status, age, ...) -- both exported

output_format='tagged_na' present on most v3 functions but absent on 10 of 51 verb-named exports: calculate_pct_time, categorize_pct_time, categorize_immigration, calculate_time_quit_smoking, calculate_SMKDSTY_original, calculate_SMKG040, calculate_SMKG203_continuous/_from_combined, calculate_SMKG207_continuous/_from_combined

Getter duplicates with divergent param names: get_variable_limits(variable_name, use_rdata) R/worksheet-getters.R:140 vs get_variable_bounds(var_name, variable_details) R/worksheet-getters.R:183-185 where roxygen line 180 admits variable_details is '(ignored, uses get_variable_limits)'
issues.why_design_issue: A DV author cannot infer whether to write height_m or HWTGHTM; the choice also changes how readable the worksheet DerivedVar:: row is and (given positional dispatch) gives no safety either way. An exported function with a documented-as-ignored parameter (get_variable_bounds) violates least surprise. Uneven output_format means some functions can emit tagged_na while siblings cannot, complicating downstream missing-data handling.
issues.candidate_fix: v4 convention: semantic snake_case parameters on all DV functions (CCHS code mapping lives in the worksheet), output_format on every DV function or centralized in the engine's post-step. Collapse get_variable_bounds into get_variable_limits with a deprecation shim and remove the ignored parameter.

issues.title: Near-duplicate exports: calculate_SMKG203_cont vs calculate_SMKG203_continuous (and 207 pair) with different signatures
evidence: R/smoke-start.R:224 calculate_SMKG203_cont <- function(SMK_005, SMKG040_cont, output_format = 'tagged_na')
R/smoking.R:787 calculate_SMKG203_continuous <- function(SMKG005, SMKG040)
R/smoke-start.R:371 calculate_SMKG207_cont <- function(SMK_030, SMKG040_cont, output_format = 'tagged_na') vs R/smoking.R:817 calculate_SMKG207_continuous <- function(SMKG005, SMKG030, SMKG040)
All four exported; only the _cont pair is referenced from variable_details.csv Func:: cells; the _continuous pair has no examples (man/calculate_SMKG203_continuous.Rd lacks \examples)
issues.why_design_issue: Two exported functions whose names differ only by abbreviation, computing the same harmonized variable from different feeder sets, is a trap: users will pick by autocomplete and get era-inappropriate logic. It also doubles maintenance for the smoking module that v3 just cleaned up.
issues.candidate_fix: Keep the worksheet-wired _cont pair; fold _continuous logic into it (or rename to express its distinct feeder era, e.g. _from_SMKG005) and deprecate the loser. Decide before v4 freeze so worksheet Func:: strings only migrate once.

issues.title: Engine and cache internals exported: ~30 infrastructure functions in the user-facing API
evidence: Cache layer (10 exports): cache_pattern, has_cached_pattern, get_cached_pattern, get_complete_pattern, get_missing_pattern, get_missing_pattern_auto, get_missing_pattern_bulk, get_variable_missing_pattern, clear_missing_patterns_cache, clear_complete_patterns_cache (R/missing-pattern-cache.R)
Heuristics/plumbing: apply_database_heuristics, auto_detect_database, extract_years_from_database_names, find_variable_in_data, assign_missing (NAMESPACE)

Engine micro-utils: is_equal(v1, v2) recode-with-table.R:33, if_else2(x, a, b) utility-functions.R:30 -- param names v1/v2/x/a/b, roxygen title 'is equal'; if_else2 is slated for deprecation in the team's derive-function standards yet still exported and load-bearing in legacy DV functions
32 exported functions have man pages with no \examples at all (mostly this infra tier); none of the cache exports appear in _pkgdown.yml
Net: a CRAN-style API review would count ~30/125 exports (24%) as internals
issues.why_design_issue: Every export is a compatibility promise; exporting the cache and heuristics layers freezes v4's freedom to redesign exactly the subsystems the refactor targets. Users browsing 125 functions cannot find the ~15 they need (rec_with_table, merge_rec_data, set_data_labels, the DV functions, worksheet getters).
issues.candidate_fix: v4: re-export only the user workflow tier; mark cache/heuristics @keywords internal (callable via ::: for power users), and replace is_equal/if_else2 usage with dplyr::case_when per the v3 standards before removal.

issues.title: rec_with_table magic defaults: deparse(substitute()) database detection, chatty messages, global-env sourcing
evidence: R/recode-with-table.R:180-183: if database_name is NULL, database_name <- deparse(substitute(data)) -- breaks under pipes (cchs2001_p |> rec_with_table() yields a non-name), wrappers, and any data frame not named exactly like a cchsflow database id

R/recode-with-table.R:171-182: three message() calls fire on a default invocation ('No variable_details detected.\n              Loading cchsflow variable_details') with embedded 14-space indentation printed to console
R/recode-with-table.R:166-169: comment 'If custom Functions are passed create new environment and source' but code is source(custom_function_path) into the global environment
Failure mode when name-guess misses: per-variable warnings at recode-with-table.R:394-409 rather than a single 'database_name not recognized; expected one of ...' error
issues.why_design_issue: Implicit name capture is fragile magic: the same call works or fails depending on what the user named their object, and the failure surfaces as dozens of confusing per-variable warnings instead of one clear error. Console noise on the happy path trains users to ignore messages.
issues.candidate_fix: v4: make database_name required (or detect from a data attribute set by a cchsflow loader); validate it against unique(databaseStart) and fail fast with the valid set; demote default-loading messages to a single rlang::inform with cli formatting; source custom functions into a new.env(parent = baseenv()).

issues.title: Examples coverage: 32 exports with no examples, 49 with only \dontrun, 23 man pages suppressing the package's own warnings
evidence: 32 exported functions' .Rd have no \examples section: includes user-facing tools get_variable_limits, get_variable_bounds, get_missing_pattern, get_smoking_variables, list_subjects, load_worksheet_metadata, calculate_time_quit_smoking (full list in audit)
49 exported functions' examples contain \dontrun{} (never executed by R CMD check), so example rot is undetected -- e.g. all 18 DOCUMENTATION ONLY stubs
23 man/*.Rd wrap examples in suppressWarnings(), e.g. man page for CCC_091_fun1 (R/number-conditions.R:27-29 roxygen: suppressWarnings(rec_with_table(...)))

Doc-stating-falsehoods: R/worksheet-getters.R:180 '@param variable_details ... (ignored, uses get_variable_limits)'; rec_with_table append_to_data/notes default inversions (recode-with-table.R:113-118 vs 160-162)
issues.why_design_issue: Untested examples and warning-suppressed examples mean the documented workflow is neither verified nor clean; new users copying the canonical example learn to silence diagnostics on day one. Missing examples on the consumer-tools tier (worksheet getters, variable discovery) undercuts the CEP-015 goal of making those tools discoverable.
issues.candidate_fix: v4 definition-of-done per exported function: runnable example against bundled cchs*_p sample data, no suppressWarnings; convert \dontrun to \donttest where runtime is the only concern; add a covr/pkgdown CI gate that fails on exported topics without examples.

issues.title: Package metadata drift: DESCRIPTION still v2.1.0 dated 2022 while exporting the v3 surface
evidence: DESCRIPTION: Version: 2.1.0, Date: 2022-05-05 in a tree whose NAMESPACE exports the v3 calculate_/assess_/clean_variables architecture
No lifecycle badges or deprecation markers anywhere (no lifecycle import in DESCRIPTION Depends/Imports block read; zero .Deprecated/lifecycle:: hits in R/)
issues.why_design_issue: Users and renv lockfiles cannot distinguish the legacy 2.1.0 API from the radically larger v3 surface; with no lifecycle signalling, every one of the 125 exports looks equally supported, which makes the planned v4 removals feel like unannounced breakage.
issues.candidate_fix: Bump to a 2.9.x/3.0.0-dev version on the v3 branch, add lifecycle to Imports, and badge every *_fun, _stub, and doc-only export as deprecated/experimental now so v4 removals are forewarned.
